### Major (revise before relaunch)

1. `scripts/issue2329_run.py:1275-1277` — cleanup can replace the original failure.

## THE NON-OBVIOUS TRAP — install kernels ⇒ RE-RUN `bank`

If the kernels are installed AFTER `bank` has captured its states (which is the
sequence the plan's refusal-response implies, since the pilot sits at P2 entry,
i.e. AFTER gates 1-2), then:

    fallback path, but
  - all subsequent generation + patching would run on the FUSED kernel path.
Fused linear-attention kernels are not bit-identical to the fallback (different
reduction order), so capture and generation would sit on two different numerical
paths. The rig has a guard for drift — `STATE_SANITY_COS_MIN = 0.99` — which is
loose enough that kernel-level differences (cos ~0.9999+) will very likely pass, so
this would NOT announce itself as a failure. That is what makes it a trap rather
than a bug: it passes quietly.
DISPOSITION if the pilot refuses and kernels go in: RE-RUN `bank` before proceeding,
so capture and generation share ONE numerical path. It costs ~6 min (the weights are
cached and bank ran in ~4 min on the resume path), which is negligible against a
~5 h run and against the alternative of a silent cross-path inconsistency
underneath every state-based read in the experiment. Do NOT rely on the sanity
check passing as evidence the paths agree — it is a drift guard, not a
path-equivalence test.

the behavior it is measuring.

## RETRACTION: the cache-staleness hazard is FALSE

I raised, and called "confirmed and serious", a hazard that re-running any judge phase
after the cap-hit re-gen would serve STALE cached scores computed on the old truncated
text. That is WRONG. What I actually confirmed was narrower — that `_item_id` is
metadata-only:
  `f"coh|anch|{row['context_id']}|{row['draw']}"`, `f"beh|anch|{cid}|{draw}|{rid}"`,
  grid `f"{block_key}|{pair_id}"`, stage2 `f"{pair_id}|{cell}|{draw}"`
— no completion text anywhere. I then INFERRED the cache was keyed on `item_id`. It is not.
`JudgeCache._hash_key` (`src/explore_persona_space/eval/batch_judge.py` ~154-165) hashes
`(key-schema version, rubric_key, question, COMPLETION)` to 16 hex. The completion text IS
in the key. The metadata-derived `item_id` serves Batch API `custom_id`s and the manifest
bijection, not cache lookup.
The tell that stopped me was arithmetic: cache filenames are 16 hex, `item_id` is a tag +
12 hex. I checked instead of acting — which is the only reason I did not send the
implementer a required cache-invalidation change it did not need, or spend a round building
one.

## What survives, and it is worth having established

1. **The re-gen needs NO cache surgery, and invalidation is exact and free.** Regenerated
   completions differ in text => different content key => cache MISS => fresh judge call;
   non-regenerated rows keep hitting. That is precisely the surgical invalidation I was
   about to hand-build. The `_JUDGE_CACHE_KEY_VERSION` component in the key gives a

`max(1, n_draws)` in the floor helper. Claude: fail-SAFE, mirrors the library. Codex: masks

MY OWN ERROR, recorded with the number because it was big: I ran a 15 GiB posix_fallocate probe to
test allocatability. It exceeded its timeout and was SIGTERMed (exit 143), which means the
`finally: os.unlink(p)` NEVER RAN -- so it left /workspace/.eps_quota_probe15 behind at 12,864 MB
(13,509,820,416 B apparent) on a pod with live compute. Had I not checked for the stray file it
would have sat there through the entire 6.4 h grid, consuming exactly the headroom I was trying to
verify, and could itself have caused the EDQUOT I was checking for. Removed (REMOVED-OK); out-root
verified back to 5,030 MB.
  LESSON, for me and for any successor: a large fallocate probe on a live pod is the wrong
  instrument twice over -- it contends for I/O with running compute, and if interrupted it LEAKS its
  full allocation because Python's `finally` does not run under SIGTERM. The safe forms are (a) a
  SMALL probe (1 GiB, which passed here in under a second) plus extrapolation from an already-measured
  footprint, or (b) a shell `trap 'rm -f "$F"' EXIT INT TERM` wrapper so the cleanup survives the
  signal. Preflight's own EDQUOT probe stays the sanctioned check; this was my ad-hoc variant.
  BETTER INSTRUMENT for the grid anyway: watch the GROWTH RATE during the run (a `du -sBM` on the
  out-root at each heartbeat is free) and act if it diverges from the ~11 GB projection. A one-shot
  upfront probe that passes tells you nothing about hour 5; continuous observation does.

THE STRUCTURAL CAUSE -- the thing I should have seen three corrections ago:
phase_grid pulls from a SHARED WORK-CONSERVING CLAIM QUEUE. So the set of COMPLETED blocks is NOT a
prefix of the block list -- it is whichever blocks happened to finish, which is biased toward the
CHEAP (short-generation) ones early and re-weights continuously as slower blocks land. Therefore
EVERY partial-set aggregate measures completion-order composition, not a property of block index, and
non-monotone wobble is guaranteed BY CONSTRUCTION. Partial reads of a claim-queue phase are biased
estimators of the final value, in an unknown direction, at every point before completion.
This single fact explains all three of my earlier misreads on this phase: the poll-6 "declining rate"
(v68, corrected v69), the "monotone cost trend" (v68, corrected v69), and now the "rising length"
(v68, preserved in error by v69, corrected here). I kept treating successive partial reads as a time
series of a stable quantity. They are not.

BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, not just a correction: I am DONE sampling the grid's length/cap-hit distribution
mid-run. The grid's own end-of-phase cap-hit report is the only unbiased read and is the number of
record. No further intermediate probes, and no ETA or cap-hit narrative built on one. (v69's rule
covered shard-RATE windows; I wrongly treated the row-level distribution as exempt because it has
n~19,500 -- large n removes SAMPLING noise but does nothing about COMPOSITION bias, which is the
error here. Precision is not accuracy.)

the gate FAILs on `rate >= threshold`, so a single parse failure survives only when
`1/n < 0.02`, i.e. `required = max(min_effective_draws_per_arm 10, floor(1/0.02) + 1) = 51`.

moment coherence passed, so I raised BOTH to the exact budget form
`n_arms * n_draws * ceil(required / n_draws) = 4 * 1 * 51 = 204` in one edit rather than
discovering the second failure on the next run.

and a clean PASS carries no evidence the true rate is under 2%). The bug was our budget, not the
gate.
